title: t2887: headless canary: validate opencode binary, detect claude CLI misconfig, long backoff on config errors
body:
alex-solovyev runner has 468 launch_recovery:no_worker_process failures in 48h because OPENCODE_BIN_DEFAULT resolves to anthropic/claude CLI (returns '2.1.119 (Claude Code)' from --version) instead of anomalyco/opencode (returns '1.14.x'). The canary then runs 'claude run -m model' which fails with 'unknown option -m' since claude CLI does not accept -m. Add pre-canary validation that detects this misconfig, searches alternative paths for a real opencode binary, falls back if found, and uses 1h backoff (vs current 90s) on structural config errors to stop the dispatch-claim spam.

title: bug: auto-decomposer-scanner re-fires on already-decomposed parents and ignores prior decision provenance
body:
## Problem

`auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` re-fires on a parent-task even when it has filed children, when the parent body still contains an `## Open questions` section that mentions an alternative the maintainer has already settled in prior closed issues.

## Real-world failure

<webapp> parent #2547 — "Self-host Tambo for AI chat interactive UI" (`parent-task`):

- Filed 2026-04-18 by maintainer with `## Open questions` section that mentioned "Vercel AI SDK as alternative — evaluate if worth it"
- That question was already settled by t011/#172 (eval DONE 2026-02-23) and t059b/#433 (Tambo self-host+rebrand DONE 2026-03-04) — but the parent body kept the legacy question text
- 2026-04-25: auto-decomposer scanner read the parent and filed three children:
  - #3044 — "Evaluate Tambo vs Vercel AI SDK" (treating the settled question as live)
  - #3045 — "Deploy and configure (Tambo OR AI SDK)"
  - #3046 — "Integrate (Tambo OR AI SDK)"
- A worker on #3044 then recommended Vercel AI SDK against the maintainer's prior directive
- Another worker on #3045 implemented Vercel AI SDK in PR <webapp>#3085 (CLOSED with CI failures)
- Maintainer reaffirmed "Tambo self-hosted please" twice on #3044 (comments 4320899245, 4321143924)
- 2026-04-26: scanner re-fired again, filing #3111 — closed today as Outcome A

Token waste: at least 5 worker dispatches across #3044/#3045/#3085 burning ~80K+ tokens total on the wrong direction.

## Root cause

`auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` checks for the `parent-task` label and the `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` nudge marker. If both are present and parent has no children section/sub-issue graph, it files a decompose request. This is correct for genuinely undecomposed parents.

The bug: when the parent IS decomposed (children exist), the scanner should not re-file. The current check appears to depend solely on the nudge-comment age vs `1-day re-file gate` from `reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`, not on whether decomposition actually exists.

A second, complementary issue: when the parent body's `## Open questions` section names an alternative the maintainer has already chosen against, the decomposer treats it as still-evaluatable. There is no "decision provenance" check.

## Proposed fix

In `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`:

1. **Skip decompose if parent already has children.** Before filing a decompose-parent issue, check:
   - Parent body has `## Children` (or `## Sub-tasks` / `## Child issues`) section with `#NNNN` references, OR
   - Parent has filed sub-issues via GitHub's sub-issue graph (GraphQL `issues(parentIssue:)`)
   - If either is true, do NOT file a decompose request — the parent is decomposed; the auto-decomposer's purpose is satisfied.

2. **Skip decompose during recent maintainer activity window.** If the parent or any child has a maintainer comment in the last 48h, skip — maintainer is engaged and will direct decomposition manually if needed.

3. **(Optional, more invasive) Decision-provenance check on `## Open questions`.** When generating the decompose body, if any prior CLOSED issue with `status:done` from the same repo links back to this parent or shares titular keywords with an open question, surface that in the decompose body so the worker doesn't re-litigate.

(1) and (2) are simple deterministic checks; (3) is the harder semantic check and probably belongs in a follow-up.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` skips parents that already have a `## Children` section listing ≥1 issue ref
- [ ] `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` skips parents with a maintainer comment in the last 48h on parent or any linked child
- [ ] Reproduction case (the <webapp> #3111 / #2547 scenario) does not re-fire after fix
- [ ] Logging: when scanner skips, emit a one-line `[skip:has-children]` or `[skip:recent-maintainer-activity]` to the scanner log so future debug is trivial

## Source repo

<webapp> — see closed #3111 (auto-decompose request) and parent #2547 for the failure trace.

## Related framework rules

- `.agents/AGENTS.md` § "Parent-task decomposition lifecycle (t2442)"
- `.agents/reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` § "AI-Generated Issue Quality (GH#17832-17835)" — same family of "scanner files issue without verifying premise" problem

## What

Reduce `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` from 0.30 (30% / 1500 points reserved) to 0.05 (5% / 250 points reserved).

## Why

The 0.30 threshold was raised from the original 0.05 in t2744 to "preserve headroom for in-flight reads" — a rationale that has since been weakened by t2689 (read-side REST fallback) shipping. title: t2899: Fix branch_orphan false-positive: workers complete on main, work discarded
body:
## What

Stop classifying successful worker completions as `worker_branch_orphan` when the worker's final HEAD ends up on the default branch (`main`/`master`). Workers exit cleanly (`exit_code=0`, `output_size=300-450KB`, `result_label=success`) and then get reclassified as orphans because `_worker_produced_output` sees `branch=main` + signal 2 fires (main exists on remote) + no PR linked → returns `branch_orphan`. Claim is released as `worker_branch_orphan` and the run is discarded.

## Why

This is the single largest current throughput sink. Evidence over the last 24h:

- 9 of 10 worker logs show `[lifecycle] worker_branch_orphan session=issue-NNN branch=main` immediately after a successful `handle_run_result_returned ... handle_exit=0 result_label=success`. (90% false-positive rate.)
- `pulse-stats.json` `counters.worker_branch_orphan_count` fired 31 times in 24h.
- `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr` failed for every observed case in the same window — recovery is broken too.
- Each false-positive discards 300-450KB of LLM output and several minutes of opus/sonnet compute. At current rate, ~20-30 worker-hours/day are wasted.

Canonical example: `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-20967.log`:

```
[INFO] [lifecycle] handle_run_result_returned session=issue-20967 handle_exit=0 result_label=success
[INFO] [lifecycle] worker_branch_orphan session=issue-20967 branch=main
[INFO] [lifecycle] Orphan recovery failed for session=issue-20967
[INFO] Released claim on #20967 (reason: worker_branch_orphan)
```

## How

Reading `_worker_produced_output` at `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1128-1197`: when `branch_name=="main"`, signal 2 (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`) ALWAYS matches because main exists on the remote. Signal 1 (`origin/main..HEAD` count) is 0 because we ARE on origin/main. Signal 3 (PR linked to issue) is 0 because no PR was opened. The function returns `branch_orphan` — which is semantically wrong: there is no orphan branch, the worker just ended on main.

Two fixes needed:

1. **EDIT `headless-runtime-helper.sh:1158-1166`** — guard signal 2 against the default branch. When `branch_name` matches the repo's default branch (resolve via `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` once and cache, fallback to env `DISPATCH_REPO_DEFAULT_BRANCH`, ultimate fallback `main`), set `has_pushed_branch=0`. Otherwise the signal is meaningless on default branches.

2. **EDIT `headless-runtime-helper.sh:1245-1278`** (`_handle_worker_branch_orphan`) — extend the diagnostic log so the next regression is debuggable. Print: original target branch (from session env if present), final HEAD, count of local commits ahead of origin, and presence of `work_dir` worktree path. This is mentorship for the next session that hits this.

3. **INVESTIGATE separately** why workers end up on main at all. The legitimate orphan is "feature branch + commits + no PR". The current pattern is "main + no commits" — that's `noop`, not `branch_orphan`. Suspected root cause: worktree-creation in `_cmd_run_prepare` is failing silently or `work_dir` is being passed as the canonical repo path. File a follow-up issue once this fix lands and we have clean diagnostic logs.

Reference pattern: `_worker_produced_output` already short-circuits to `noop` at line 1168-1172 when both signals are absent. The fix extends that early-exit logic.

## Acceptance

- After deploy: `worker_branch_orphan_count` over a 24h window drops below 10% of completed workers (current: 90%). Measure: `cat ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json | jq '(.counters.worker_branch_orphan_count | length)'` 24h delta.
- New diagnostic log line on every orphan classification includes target_branch, final_head, ahead_count, work_dir.
- Legitimate orphan path (real feature branch + commits + no PR) still triggers `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr`. Verified by unit test.
- New test file `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh` covers:
  - `branch=main, ahead=0, no PR` → returns `noop`
  - `branch=main, ahead=N, no PR` → returns `noop` (default-branch guard)
  - `branch=feature/tNNN-foo, ahead=N, no PR` → returns `branch_orphan` (unchanged)
  - `branch=feature/tNNN-foo, ahead=N, PR exists` → returns `pr_exists` (unchanged)

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh
- .agents/AGENTS.md

## Complexity Impact

`_worker_produced_output` is 70 lines today (1128-1197). Adding the default-branch guard adds ~10 lines → 80 lines. Within the 80-100 advisory window; no refactor required.

## Verification

```

.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh
# Then watch for 24h:
jq '.counters.worker_branch_orphan_count | length' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json
```

title: t2902: Stop recurring GraphQL budget exhaustion despite REST fallback (t2574, t2689)
body:
## What

Stop the recurring GraphQL budget exhaustion. The GraphQL pool resets to 5000/hour and is being driven to 0 between resets, tripping the pulse circuit breaker (5% threshold) and pausing all dispatch. Observed 11 fires in the last 24h, 47 lifetime. Each fire pauses the entire dispatch path for whatever fraction of the hour remains until reset.

## Why

Right now (snapshot during this session): `gh api rate_limit` returns `{graphql: 0/5000, core: 4256/5000, search: 30/30}`. So:

- Core REST has 4256 of 5000 left — REST-routed ops are healthy.
- Search has 30/30 fresh — `gh search` ops ARE expensive in points (30 budget, 30 in use is unrelated to the GraphQL pool but is a separate scarce resource).
- GraphQL is fully drained.

The framework already has REST fallback for write paths (t2574 — `gh_create_issue`, `gh_create_pr`, etc.) and read paths (t2689 — issue list, PR view). With both routed, GraphQL should NOT be drained. Yet it is. So at least one heavy GraphQL consumer is not using either fallback.

Suspect call sites (need verification):

1. **`gh search issues|prs`** (`pulse-batch-prefetch`, `auto-decomposer-helper.sh`, `pulse-merge.sh`) — `gh search` uses GraphQL Search API and is documented to cost 30+ points per query against the GraphQL pool, not Search's 30/min token bucket. `~/.aidevops/logs/contribution-watch.log` shows this is the failing operation: "[pulse-batch-prefetch] gh search issues failed for owner=marcusquinn: GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded".
2. **`gh pr view --json checks`** — uses GraphQL when checks include status checks + check-runs aggregation.
3. **`preflight_ownership_reconcile` 124 errors** — strong correlation with GraphQL exhaustion. Stage may be re-trying GraphQL queries that already failed earlier in the cycle.

## How

Three steps:

### Step 1: instrument

Add to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (or wherever the auto-router lives) a counter that increments per call site, partitioned by `path` (REST vs GraphQL). Dump to `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json` once per pulse cycle. After 1 cycle of data, we know exactly who the heavy consumer is. Without this we are guessing.

### Step 2: route or cache the offender

Once instrumentation identifies the heavy consumer:

- If it's `gh search`: replace with a per-repo `gh issue list --search "<query>"` REST-backed loop where possible. Cost: more REST calls (cheaper), more wall time. Benefit: no GraphQL pressure.
- If it's `gh pr view --json checks`: split into two calls (`gh pr view --json basic` REST + `gh api repos/.../check-runs/...` REST) and reassemble.
- For repeated reads of slowly-changing data: add a 5-min disk cache keyed by `(owner, repo, op, args_hash)`. Existing pattern: `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt` proves the cache idiom is in use.

### Step 3: lower the floor (operational mitigation, not the fix)

The breaker threshold is 5% (250/5000). Effective when budget is healthy; useless when consumption rate exceeds regeneration. Consider raising the soft fallback threshold (`AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD`, default 1000) to 1500 — earlier REST fallback gives more headroom. This is a one-line config change pending the real fix from steps 1-2.

Reference pattern: `shared-gh-wrappers.sh::_gh_wrapper_auto_route` already inspects rate limits before each write call and routes accordingly. Same logic should apply to read calls and to `gh search` substitution.

## Acceptance

- After fix: `gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining'` stays above 1000 for 24h continuous observation.
- `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` counter increments at most 1x per 24h (current: 11/24h, 47 lifetime).
- `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json` exists and shows GraphQL routes only for ops with no REST equivalent (e.g., addSubIssue, GraphQL-only mutations).

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
- .agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-helper.sh
- .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf

## Complexity Impact

`shared-gh-wrappers.sh` already has the routing infrastructure (t2574, t2689). Step 1 (instrumentation) is ~30 lines. Step 2 (per-offender routing) is bounded by the number of offenders found — likely 2-3. Step 3 (threshold) is one line. No function should grow past 100 lines.

## Verification

```

cat ~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls-by-stage.json | jq 'to_entries | sort_by(-.value.graphql_calls)'

# 24h GraphQL floor:
while true; do gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining'; sleep 600; done | tee /tmp/gql-floor.log
# Floor should never drop below 1000.

# Circuit fire rate:
jq '.counters.pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken | map(select(. > (now - 86400))) | length' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json
```

title: t2904: Cache assignment graph + classify errors in preflight_ownership_reconcile
body:
## What

Investigate why `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` (in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, around line 1251) takes 602s with 124 errors per pulse cycle. Reduce both: (a) cache the assignment graph between cycles with a 5-minute TTL so unchanged-state cycles short-circuit; (b) classify errors so rate-limit retries trip the circuit breaker once instead of accumulating to 124 per cycle.

## Why

`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log` for 2026-04-26 14:41:46Z: `preflight_ownership_reconcile	602	124	28101` — 602s wall-clock, 124 errors on a single cycle. This is the single largest stage cost after `complexity_scan` (471s) and combined they consume 60% of the 1800s pulse stale ceiling.

124 errors is too high to be repo-coverage. Hypotheses (need confirmation in the diagnostic step below):
1. Rate-limit retries: each 401/403/secondary-rate hits the catch-all path and counts as one error.
2. Permission errors on archived/private repos that get re-queried each cycle.
3. The reconciler re-reads the same data across multiple sub-stages.

A 5-min TTL cache on the assignment graph would cover the case where consecutive pulse cycles see identical state. With t2901 Track 2 raising `StartInterval` to 600s, two consecutive cycles often see no assignment changes — perfect for cache hits.

## How

### Diagnostic First (before implementation)

Add a short-lived debug trace to `_preflight_ownership_reconcile`. Write each error-path event to `~/.aidevops/logs/ownership-reconcile-debug.log` with: timestamp, repo slug, API call (or sub-function), HTTP/exit status, error text. Run for 2-3 pulse cycles. Aggregate:

```bash
awk '{print $4}' ~/.aidevops/logs/ownership-reconcile-debug.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

The top error class drives the design choices below. Remove the trace before merging.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — locate `_preflight_ownership_reconcile` (search for the function definition; line 1251 was the t2901 reference). Add cache check at function entry. Cache key: sha256 of `(repo slug + last status:* label timestamp)` per repo. Cache file: `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/cache/ownership-graph-<sha>.json`, TTL 300s (5 min).
- EDIT: same file — error classification: when an API call fails, check exit code. `gh` exit 4 = rate-limit (set a flag, abort the stage early, let pulse circuit breaker handle). Other non-zero = generic error (log once per repo at WARN level, don't increment the per-call error counter on each retry within a single repo).
- VERIFY (read-only): `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` — confirm what data the ownership reconciler depends on. If these helpers cache their own results inside one cycle, the reconciler may be able to consume that cache instead of re-calling `gh`.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ownership-reconcile-cache.sh` — exercise cache-hit and cache-miss paths with controlled state files. Add to the test runner.

### Reference Pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh:752` — `check_repo_pulse_interval` uses a state file with mtime-based TTL. Same shape: read state file, compare mtime to TTL, decide skip vs. re-run.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` — batches multiple `gh` calls and caches results for the cycle. Use this for the cache-miss path: fetch the assignment graph in one batched call, write to cache, return.
- `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — search for `RATE_LIMIT` / exit-code-4 handling for the error-classification pattern: detect once, set a flag, return early.

## Acceptance

- After deploy: `preflight_ownership_reconcile` cost drops below 60s on cycles where no repo has status-label changes (cache-hit path).
- After deploy: error count drops below 10 per cycle (down from 124).
- Cache invalidation is correct: a real assignment change is reflected within one TTL window (manual test: change a status label on a repo, verify reconciler picks it up within 5 min).
- New test passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-ownership-reconcile-cache.sh`.

awk -F'\t' '$2 == "preflight_ownership_reconcile" {print $1, $3, $4}' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -10
# Expected: most cycles show <60s, error count <10.

title: t2905: Audit prefetch_state cost vs downstream savings (184s/cycle)
body:
## What

Audit `prefetch_state` stage in the pulse cycle (currently 184s per cycle per `pulse-stage-timings.log`). Verify that the work it does saves more than 184s downstream. If not, remove it or downscope it. If yes, document the value-vs-cost trade-off so future audits can find the rationale.

## Why

`pulse-stage-timings.log` shows `prefetch_state` consistently around 184s. That's 3.1 minutes of every pulse cycle. The stage exists to batch-fetch state from `gh` (issues, PRs, labels) so downstream stages don't have to re-fetch. The hypothesis when it was added: cost-amortisation across many downstream stages > one-time fetch cost.

We don't have evidence that this hypothesis still holds. Three classes of work that could invalidate it:

1. **Read-side REST fallback (t2689)**: many downstream `gh` calls now route via REST (the separate 5000/hr pool) when GraphQL is constrained. If REST calls are no longer rate-limited, the prefetch may be saving zero downstream cost.
2. **Cache hits (proposed t2901 Track 1b)**: if the ownership reconciler starts caching its own result, it doesn't need prefetch_state at all.
3. **Dispatch-dedup REST fallback (#20991, t2689)**: dispatch-dedup `is-assigned` already hits REST under load. Same concern.

## How

### Files Scope

- READ-ONLY first: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` — understand what data prefetch_state is actually fetching. Search for the `prefetch_state` stage entry point in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (look for `run_stage_with_timeout "prefetch_state"`).
- READ-ONLY: every downstream stage that consumes prefetched data — `_preflight_capacity_and_labels`, `_preflight_ownership_reconcile`, `_preflight_cleanup_and_ledger`, dispatch loop. Identify by searching for `read_prefetched_state` / `PULSE_STATE_DIR` / equivalent variable.

### Audit (no code changes yet)

Add temporary timing instrumentation:
1. Wrap each downstream consumer call with `time` and log the duration to `~/.aidevops/logs/prefetch-consumer-timings.log`.
2. Run for 5-10 pulse cycles.
3. Sum the consumer time per cycle. Compare to 184s prefetch cost.

If `prefetch_total_consumer_time < 184s` over the sample window: prefetch_state is a net cost — remove it (each downstream consumer makes its own call, possibly with REST fallback).

If `prefetch_total_consumer_time > 184s × 3` (3x rule of thumb for amortised value): prefetch_state is genuinely saving time — leave it, document the savings in the function header comment.

If `184s < prefetch_total < 184s × 3`: marginal value. Lean toward removal because the cost is observable and the savings are small.

### Files Scope (depending on audit outcome)

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — if removing: drop the `run_stage_with_timeout "prefetch_state"` call. If keeping: add a comment block explaining the cost-vs-value rationale measured during this audit.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` — if removing: keep the helper functions but remove the orchestrator. If keeping: no changes.
- EDIT: any downstream consumer that depends on prefetched state — if removing prefetch, switch them to direct calls (likely already supported via cache miss path).

### Reference Pattern

- `pulse-stage-timings.log` is the canonical source for cost measurement.
- `reference/observability.md` describes the OTEL span enrichment pattern; if removing prefetch_state, the OTEL span for the stage will disappear from the logs — this is fine but should be noted in the PR body.

## Acceptance

- One of the following two outcomes is shipped:
  - **Outcome A (remove)**: `prefetch_state` no longer appears in `pulse-stage-timings.log`. Total cycle duration drops by ≥184s. Downstream stages still pass their tests.
  - **Outcome B (keep + document)**: `prefetch_state` remains; `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` orchestrator function header includes a comment block measuring the savings ratio (e.g. "Prefetch costs 184s, saves 600s of downstream calls per cycle = 3.3x value").
- The audit log (`~/.aidevops/logs/prefetch-consumer-timings.log` analysis) is summarised in the PR body so the rationale survives.

## Verification

awk '$2 == "prefetch_state"' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -5
# Expected: no fresh entries.

awk '/^[0-9]/ {if (max < $1) max = $1; if (min == 0 || min > $1) min = $1} END {print min, max}' \
  ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log | tail -5
# Expected: total cycle duration dropped by ~184s.

# After deploy (Outcome B):
grep -A 5 "prefetch_state cost" .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh
# Expected: header comment with measured savings ratio.

title: t2908: setup.sh non-interactive resilience: caching, instrumentation, lock recovery
body:
## What

`setup.sh --non-interactive` is the auto-update deploy path. It currently has three structural risks that combine into a silent-failure mode for the framework:

1. **Excess work on every cycle.** Non-interactive setup takes ~6.5 min total; ~135s of that is regenerable content that should be skipped on unchanged input.
2. **No per-stage observability.** A hang in any of ~93 sequential steps is invisible in the auto-update log — diagnosis requires a `bash -x` reproduction.
3. **No stale-lock recovery.** If the lock holder process is alive but wedged, the lock is held indefinitely and auto-update silently stops working until a maintainer notices and clears `~/.aidevops/.autoupdate.lock` by hand.

This is a parent issue tracking three independent fixes (one issue each) plus an explicitly-deferred fourth question (per-stage hard timeout, decision blocked on Phase B data).

## Why (measured)

Reproduced on this machine (2026-04-26) with `gtimeout 600 bash -x ./setup.sh --non-interactive` and per-line `EPOCHREALTIME` tracing. Total wall time: ~390s (~6.5 min). Top stages:

| Stage | Wall time | File |
|---|---|---|
| `generate-runtime-config.sh all --runtime claude-code` | 78.97s | `setup-modules/config.sh:95` |
| `generate-skills.sh` | 71.49s | `setup-modules/plugins.sh:225` |
| `generate-runtime-config.sh all --runtime opencode` | 57.02s | `setup-modules/config.sh:95` |
| `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running` | 6.79s | `setup.sh:1317` |
| `cch-extract.sh --cache` | 4.64s | `setup.sh:1161` |
| 9× `routine-log-helper.sh refresh-description rNNN` | 3.45–4.30s each (~36s total) | `init-routines-helper.sh:786` |

`generate-skills.sh` already implements input-hash caching (`~/.aidevops/agents/.skills-source-hash`, `generate-skills.sh:253-280`). `generate-runtime-config.sh` does not — its 135.99s combined cost is recurring on every auto-update tick, not justified by changed inputs.

The auto-update path runs on a launchd timer (~10 min cadence). 6.5 min of work on a 10 min cadence means ~65% duty cycle on the deploy path even when nothing has changed upstream. On slower machines this exceeds the cadence and stacks behind the lock.

`auto-update-helper.sh` invokes setup.sh with `bash "$INSTALL_DIR/setup.sh" --non-interactive >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1` — no timeout wrapper, no per-stage timing emitted. The only timeouts in the auto-update path are `curl --max-time 10` for the version probe (lines 351, 363). Everything else hangs forever on the original failure mode.

## Decomposition

Four sub-issues (3 filed for autonomous implementation, 1 deferred):

| Phase | Title | Issue | Cost saved / risk addressed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Input-hash cache for `generate-runtime-config.sh` | (filed below) | ~135s/cycle |
| B | Structured per-stage timing log | (filed below) | Foundation for Phase D — current logs reveal nothing |
| C | Stale-lock recovery in auto-update-helper.sh | (filed below) | Recovers from wedged lock holder |
| D | Per-stage hard timeout in non-interactive path | DEFERRED | Wraps every external/long step in `timeout`; design depends on Phase B telemetry to identify which stages can fail-loud-and-skip safely vs. must-succeed-or-abort |

## Acceptance gate (this issue closes when)

- All three filed children (A, B, C) merge.
- Reproducing the trace on this machine shows total non-interactive setup time below 4 min on an unchanged-input run (target: ~250s, dominated by stages we are NOT optimising).
- 24h auto-update log captures structured per-stage timing for at least one cycle.
- Stale-lock recovery test passes: kill the lock holder mid-update, confirm auto-update self-recovers within the configured stale threshold.

Phase D will be filed as a separate parent if Phase B data warrants it. Closing this parent does not require Phase D.

## Verification commands (paste any time)

```bash
# Total non-interactive setup wall time
( time bash ~/Git/aidevops/setup.sh --non-interactive >/tmp/setup.log 2>&1 ) 2>&1 | tail -3

# Per-stage timing trace (after Phase B lands)
tail -50 ~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log

# Auto-update lock state
ls -la ~/.aidevops/.autoupdate.lock 2>&1 | head -3
```

## Related

- t2906 (#21054) — atomic plist write — shipped in parallel; same session, same root surface (setup.sh deploy path), but addresses the *symptom* (corrupted artefact on hang). This issue addresses the *risk surface* (preventing the hang in the first place + recovering from it).
- t2901 (#21042) — pulse cycle decomposition — same diagnostic shape (single composite issue → measured evidence → 3 phase children).

title: t2909: Auto-release path leaves status:in-review and self-assignment on GitHub
body:
## What

Make `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale --auto-release` (Phase 1, t2414) actually clear the GitHub-side claim, not just the local stamp file. The current implementation deletes the stamp on disk but leaves `status:in-review` and the self-assignee in place on GitHub, which leaves the footprint-overlap cache (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`) treating those issues as in-flight forever and blocking dispatch on every issue that touches an overlapping file path.

## Why

Direct evidence from this morning's session:

1. Ran `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale --auto-release` — output: `Phase 1 auto-released 16 stamp(s).`
2. Confirmed local stamps gone: `ls ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/claim-stamps/` returns nothing.
3. **Verified 14 of those 16 issues STILL carry `status:in-review` + `assignees=marcusquinn` on GitHub** (the other two were #20898 merged and #21026 closed-by-merge, both legitimately cleared by other code paths):

   ```
   20895 OPEN assignees=marcusquinn labels=status:in-review,origin:interactive
   20896 OPEN assignees=marcusquinn labels=status:in-review,origin:interactive
   20897 OPEN assignees=marcusquinn labels=status:in-review,origin:interactive
   20899-20905, 20908-20912 — all the same pattern
   ```

4. `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` since the fix landed shows ~20 dispatch deferrals with `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#20895 ...)`, `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#20896 ...)`, `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#20897 ...)` — every issue that mentions `pulse-wrapper.sh` or `setup.sh` in its body is being blocked because the footprint cache thinks those three (and 11 others) are still being worked on.

Reading the code:

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:1110-1129` (`_isc_release_claim_by_stamp_path`) — the Phase 1 auto-release entry point. Comment claims it "delegates to `_isc_cmd_release` which handles stamp deletion and label transition atomically".
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:766-850` (`_isc_cmd_release`) — has TWO failure modes that produce this exact symptom:
  - Line 818: `_isc_has_in_review` lookup can return 2 (read failed); if so, line 824-826 skips the label transition with only a warning.
  - Line 843-846: `set_issue_status ... available` is called but errors are silenced via `>/dev/null 2>&1`; on failure the user sees only `release: gh failed on #$issue — label may still be set`.
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:834-841`: `--unassign` is opt-in. `_isc_release_claim_by_stamp_path` does NOT pass `--unassign`. So even when the label transition succeeds, the assignee stays. The dedup invariant `(active label) AND (non-self assignee)` (t1996) means this only fully unblocks if the label clears AND the runner login is treated as "non-self" elsewhere — for owner-self-claims, the assignee alone keeps dispatch blocked per GH#18352.

So Phase 1 auto-release has a triple flaw:

1. It delegates without `--unassign`, so even a perfectly-functioning label transition leaves a permanent dispatch block via owner self-assignment.
2. The label transition itself silently no-ops on read errors and silently fails on write errors — no remediation, no retry, no log line that surfaces in `pulse-wrapper.log`.
3. The footprint cache (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:108-188`) re-queries `gh issue list --label status:in-review --state open` every 120s. As long as the GitHub label is stuck, every cache rebuild produces the same poisoned data — TTL doesn't help.

The footprint cache is correct as designed. The bug is upstream in the release path.

## How

Three coordinated changes:

### 1. `_isc_release_claim_by_stamp_path` must pass `--unassign`

EDIT `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:1127` — change `_isc_cmd_release "$r_issue" "$r_slug"` to `_isc_cmd_release --unassign "$r_issue" "$r_slug"`. Auto-release is by definition the dead-stamp recovery path; the runner that owned it is gone, so the assignment is meaningless and must clear. Phase 2 (closed-PR orphans) and the manual `release` fallback are different — those keep their current opt-in semantics.

### 2. Surface release failures, don't silence them

EDIT `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:843` — replace the silenced `set_issue_status ... >/dev/null 2>&1` with a captured-stderr pattern that prints the gh error on failure:

```bash
local _set_status_err
_set_status_err=$(set_issue_status "$issue" "$slug" "available" \
    ${extra_flags[@]+"${extra_flags[@]}"} 2>&1 >/dev/null)
local _set_status_rc=$?
if [[ $_set_status_rc -eq 0 ]]; then
    _isc_info "release: #$issue → status:available"
    return 0
fi
_isc_warn "release: gh failed on #$issue (rc=$_set_status_rc): $_set_status_err"
return 0
```

The current pattern hid the actual cause of the 14 stuck issues for the entire morning.

### 3. Add a one-shot reconciler — heal already-stuck claims

NEW: `.agents/scripts/scripts/reconcile-stuck-claims.sh` — scans every `pulse:true` repo for issues matching `(origin:interactive) AND (status:in-review OR status:claimed) AND (assignee=$current_user) AND (no live stamp at ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/claim-stamps/<slug>-<num>.json)`. For each match, calls `_isc_cmd_release --unassign $num $slug`. Idempotent. Surfaces any release failures verbatim (consequence of #2). Dry-run by default; `--apply` to commit. Designed to be run once after this fix lands to clear the existing backlog, and then occasionally as a safety net.

Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/reconcile-origin-labels.sh` is the existing one-shot reconciliation idiom (t2200). Same structure, same `--dry-run`/`--apply` UX.

## Acceptance

- After fix deploy + reconciler run-once: zero issues match the stuck-claim query above. Verify with the reconciler in `--dry-run` mode.
- Synthetic test: `tests/test-stamp-release-github-gap.sh` — creates a fake stamp, marks an issue `status:in-review` with self-assignee, runs `scan-stale --auto-release`, asserts the GitHub issue is `status:available` AND has no self-assignee. Run against a sandbox repo or use a mocked `gh` shim.
- Direct dispatch unblocking: 24h after deploy, `pulse.log` shows zero `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#20895 ...)` / `#20896` / `#20897` entries (currently ~20 in the last hour).
- `_isc_cmd_release` failure path now prints the actual `gh` error to stderr — verify by sabotaging a release call (revoke gh token temporarily) and reading the warning.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/reconcile-stuck-claims.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-stamp-release-github-gap.sh

## Complexity Impact

- `_isc_release_claim_by_stamp_path` change is a 1-line delta (add `--unassign`).
- `_isc_cmd_release` change is a 6-line delta around line 843 (capture stderr, surface on failure). Function is currently 84 lines (766-850); post-change ~90 lines. Within 80-100 advisory window.
- `reconcile-stuck-claims.sh` is a new file modelled on `reconcile-origin-labels.sh`, expected ~120-150 lines.

## Verification

```
# Before deploy: confirm the stuck set matches the brief
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --label "status:in-review" --assignee "@me" \
    --search "is:open" --json number,labels --jq '.[].number'

# After deploy + reconciler:
.agents/scripts/reconcile-stuck-claims.sh --dry-run
# Expected: "No stuck claims found."

# After 24h:
rg -c "FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP \(issue=#2089[5-9]" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
# Expected: 0
```

title: Address PR #21062 review feedback: mv check, legacy cleanup, mktemp, empty guard
body:
## What

Address review concerns raised on PR #21062 (t2906 atomic plist install) that were filed as additive follow-ups to ship the core fix on time.

## Why

PR #21062 fixed a critical 0-byte plist bug via atomic tmp+rename. Bot reviews flagged 4 secondary correctness/hygiene issues that didn't block the core fix but should be addressed for production safety.

## How

Fix in priority order:

### Priority 1 — `mv` exit status not checked (gemini HIGH, augmentcode HIGH)

`setup.sh:257`. Current:
```bash
mv -f "$tmp_plist" "$plist_path"
launchctl load "$plist_path" 2>/dev/null || return 1
```
If `mv` fails, `launchctl load` may succeed against the old plist and the function returns 0 (silent no-op).

EDIT `setup.sh:257`: capture and check mv exit:
```bash
if ! mv -f "$tmp_plist" "$plist_path"; then
    rm -f "$tmp_plist"
    return 1
fi
```

### Priority 2 — restore legacy plist cleanup (gemini MEDIUM, augmentcode MEDIUM)

`setup-modules/schedulers.sh:686`. The PR removed `_cleanup_old_pulse_plists` which handled the one-time migration from `com.aidevops.supervisor-pulse.plist` (legacy label) to `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` (current label). Users on stale installs could end up with both loaded → 2x dispatch.

EDIT `_install_pulse_launchd`: re-add a guarded legacy cleanup BEFORE the `_launchd_install_if_changed` call. Only target the hardcoded legacy path; don't touch the current path. Idempotent — no-op when legacy isn't present.

### Priority 3 — temp filename predictability (gemini SECURITY-MEDIUM)

`setup.sh:246`. `${plist_path}.tmp.$$` is predictable; symlink-attack risk in `/tmp` style locations (here it's `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` so risk is low — userland). Use `mktemp` for defense in depth:
```bash
local tmp_plist
tmp_plist=$(mktemp "${plist_path}.XXXXXX") || return 1
```

### Priority 4 — empty content guard (augmentcode MEDIUM)

`setup.sh:253`. `[[ ! -s "$tmp_plist" ]]` checks file size after `printf '%s\n'` (which writes a trailing newline = 1 byte for empty content). Doesn't catch empty `$new_content`.

EDIT: check `$new_content` directly before write:
```bash
if [[ -z "$new_content" ]]; then
    rm -f "$tmp_plist"
    return 1
fi
```

## Acceptance

- All 4 priorities addressed in a single PR.
- Tests: synthetic `tests/test-launchd-install-if-changed.sh` covers (a) mv-failure path returns 1, (b) legacy cleanup runs once, (c) empty content rejected.
- Bot reviews on the new PR show 0 unaddressed HIGH/MEDIUM findings.

## Files Scope

- setup.sh
- setup-modules/schedulers.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-launchd-install-if-changed.sh

## Verification

```bash
bash -n setup.sh
shellcheck setup.sh setup-modules/schedulers.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-launchd-install-if-changed.sh
```

title: t2913: Move gh wall-clock timeouts into wrapper layer (replaces #21038)
body:
## What

Move wall-clock timeouts from leaf call sites in `stats-health-dashboard.sh` (PR #21038) into the wrapper layer in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. Replaces the 7-call-site sprinkle with a single chokepoint that all callers benefit from automatically — and preserves the t2689 REST fallback that #21038 inadvertently regressed at 2 sites.

Context: PR #21038 was opened against `superdav42/tgc.church` indefinitely-stalling `gh issue list` calls observed in `Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent#1192`. The diagnosis (gh has no native timeout, processes can wedge in TCP) is correct; the fix location is wrong. PR #21038 is closing in favour of this issue.

## Why

The PR's approach has four problems:

1. **Coverage gap** — patches 7 of N call sites in one file. Every other consumer of `gh_issue_list` / `gh_issue_view` / `gh_pr_list` (15+ scripts, including `pulse-merge.sh`, `pulse-cleanup.sh`, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`) is still unprotected.
2. **t2689 regression** — replaces `gh_issue_list` with raw `timeout 30 gh issue list` at 2 sites in `stats-health-dashboard.sh`, dropping the REST-fallback path t2689 (PR #20332, merged 5 days ago) added specifically for those sites under GraphQL rate-limit pressure.
3. **Magic 30** — same number for read (`issue list`, p99 ~5s) and write (`issue edit`, p99 ~10-15s) operations. Reads should fail fast (~3× p99); writes deserve more headroom because they cannot be safely retried.
4. **No observability** — when timeout fires, falls through to `|| echo "0"`. Caller cannot distinguish "API legitimately returned 0" from "call wedged for 30s and we gave up".

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` — add `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT` (default 15s) and `AIDEVOPS_GH_WRITE_TIMEOUT` (default 45s) defaults with rationale comment
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — add `_gh_with_timeout` helper near top; modify `gh_issue_view`, `gh_pr_list`, `gh_issue_list` to invoke primary `gh ...` via the helper
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` — wrap inner `gh api` calls in `_rest_issue_view`, `_rest_pr_list`, `_rest_issue_list` with the helper

### Reference pattern

Model the helper on existing config-loading pattern in `pulse-wrapper-config.sh:99-106` (env var takes precedence over conf file via `${VAR:-default}`). Model wrapper integration on the existing `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` chokepoint in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:1714-1722` — same place, additive.

### Design

```bash
# In shared-gh-wrappers.sh near line 90 (after instrumentation source):

: "${AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT:=15}"   # idempotent reads
: "${AIDEVOPS_GH_WRITE_TIMEOUT:=45}"  # non-idempotent writes

_gh_with_timeout() {
    local op_class="$1"; shift
    local secs
    case "$op_class" in
        read)  secs="${AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT}" ;;
        write) secs="${AIDEVOPS_GH_WRITE_TIMEOUT}" ;;
        *)     secs=30 ;;
    esac
    if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        timeout "$secs" "$@"
        return $?
    fi
    "$@"
    return $?
}
```

Then in each read wrapper, replace `gh issue list "$@"` → `_gh_with_timeout read gh issue list "$@"`, and similarly for view/pr-list. In each `_rest_*` translator, replace `gh api "$_path"` → `_gh_with_timeout read gh api "$_path"`.

Every shell function MUST have an explicit `return 0` or `return 1` (TTSR rule, SonarCloud S7682).

### Why these timeout values

- **Read 15s** = ~3× observed p99 for `gh issue list` on healthy days. Long enough to absorb GitHub API slow days, short enough that a wedged TCP connection is caught well before user-visible delay accumulates.
- **Write 45s** = ~3× p99 for `gh issue edit` (validation + webhook fanout). Higher headroom because writes cannot be safely retried (`gh issue comment` twice = duplicate comments).
- **Configurable** = env vars override conf file; runners with slow networks or unusually large `--limit` values can tune up.

### Out of scope

- Retry logic (will be a separate task once we have observability data on read-timeout frequency).
- Write-side wrapper timeouts (`gh_issue_edit_safe`, `gh_pr_edit_safe`, etc.) — focused diff. Reads are the demonstrated failure mode; writes can follow.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_gh_with_timeout` helper exists in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` with explicit `return` statements

title: t2916: worktree sweep: consult interactive-session claim stamps in should_skip_cleanup
body:
<!-- Task: t2916 ref:GH#21074 -->

## Task

Add interactive-session claim-stamp consultation to `should_skip_cleanup()` in `worktree-helper.sh` so `wt clean` / `r005` daily worktree cleanup never trashes a worktree whose linked GitHub issue has an active interactive claim.

## Why

Two incidents in one day (2026-04-26):

1. **t2913 worktree** sent to `~/.Trash` immediately before the user resumed the session. Recovery: restore from trash + `git worktree add`.
2. **t2903 worktree** sent to `~/.Trash` mid-session **after** PR #21070 was opened with an `origin:interactive` label. Recovery: same.

Each loss costs ~2-5 min recovery + breaks the user's flow + creates the impression that worktrees are unreliable. Three `~/.Trash` recoveries this month (with possibly more we missed). Root cause is structural: the safety gate has no signal for "an interactive session owns this work right now", so it relies on proxies (open-PR check, dirty-files check, 4h grace period) that all have failure modes.

## How

`worktree-helper.sh::should_skip_cleanup` (`.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh:1439-1505`) currently has 4 safety checks: PID-ownership (t189), 4h grace period, open-PR list, and zero-commit-dirty. NONE consult the canonical interactive-session claim-stamp directory at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-session-claims/<slug-flat>-<issue>.json` — even though the dispatch-dedup gate already trusts the same source.

Each existing check has a known failure mode that lets active work through:

- **PID-ownership** depends on entries in `worktree-registry.db` SQLite. Manual `git worktree add` (e.g., during trash-recovery) does NOT register; pruned-stale entries fail open. Both observed today.
- **4h grace** is a cliff — work that takes >4h hits it. t2903 was created at ~16:30 UTC, swept ~17:30 — so likely also a `gh pr list` failure case below, not grace.
- **Open-PR check** depends on `_clean_build_open_pr_branches` (= `gh pr list`). On rate-limit or transient network errors it returns empty — silent fail-open. PR #21070 was open and labeled `origin:interactive`; the check still passed-through.
- **Zero-commit-dirty** is narrow (only fires when 0 commits ahead AND uncommitted files).

Additionally, `_clean_classify_worktree` Check 2 (`branch_was_pushed && ! _branch_exists_on_any_remote`) can fire spuriously if `git fetch --prune` races with a push: the local ref-cache shows "no remote branch" momentarily even though origin has it. The `remote_unknown=false` guard at `:1610` only catches outright fetch failure, not transient prune races.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`
- `tests/test-worktree-cleanup-claim-guard.sh` (NEW)

### Files to modify

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`** — add a sourceable lookup function `_isc_branch_has_active_claim <branch>` that:
  - Maps `feature/tNNN-...` or `feature/gh-NNN-...` branch → issue number (mirror `worktree-helper.sh:_extract_issue_from_branch` if present, else add this helper there too).
  - Maps repo path → slug via existing `_isc_slug_flat`.
  - Reads `$(_isc_stamp_path issue slug)` and returns 0 if file exists with `pid` field referencing a live process (`kill -0 $pid 2>/dev/null`); otherwise 1.
  - Add `--branch <ref>` CLI surface for shell consumers that want a portable check without sourcing.
- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh:1439-1505`** — insert a 5th check at the top of `should_skip_cleanup` (before the 4h grace cliff so claim-stamp wins even on stale work):

  ```bash
  # Active claim check (THIS-TASK-ID): skip if interactive-session
  # claim-stamp exists for this branch's issue with a live PID. Same
  # source of truth as the dispatch-dedup gate.
  if command -v _isc_branch_has_active_claim >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if _isc_branch_has_active_claim "$wt_branch"; then
      echo -e "  ${RED}$wt_branch${NC} (active interactive claim - skipping)"
      echo "    $wt_path"
      echo ""
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  ```

  Source `interactive-session-helper.sh` near the top of `worktree-helper.sh` (where other helpers are sourced) using the same conditional pattern as existing sources.
- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`** — verify the same guard is reachable. The pulse-cleanup path may have its own `_trash_or_remove` allowlist (added by t2559) — extend it to honour the claim-stamp check too, or document why it doesn't apply.
- **NEW: `tests/test-worktree-cleanup-claim-guard.sh`** — three tests:
  1. Worktree with claim-stamp + live PID → skipped.
  2. Worktree with claim-stamp + dead PID → swept (stale).
  3. No claim-stamp → existing behaviour preserved (regression guard).

### Reference pattern

Follow the existing `is_worktree_owned_by_others` pattern at `worktree-helper.sh:1447-1456` for the print/return shape. Follow `_isc_stamp_path` and `_isc_write_stamp` patterns in `interactive-session-helper.sh` for the lookup shape — keep the new function `_isc_*` prefixed.

### Verification

```bash

# 2. Live test: create a worktree, claim its issue, run wt clean --auto
worktree-helper.sh add feature/test-claim-guard --issue 99999
interactive-session-helper.sh claim 99999 marcusquinn-aidevops
worktree-helper.sh clean --auto --force-merged

# 3. Shellcheck

```

`should_skip_cleanup` is currently ~67 lines (1439-1505). Adding the new check adds ~10 lines including conditional sourcing. Projected post-change: ~77 lines — well under the 100-line `function-complexity` gate. No refactor required.

`_isc_branch_has_active_claim` is a new function projected at ~25-30 lines. Under all gates.

- [ ] `_isc_branch_has_active_claim` function added to `interactive-session-helper.sh` with both sourceable and CLI surfaces.

title: t2917: Runner scripts hardcode $HOME/.aidevops/logs but plist/timer installers resolve paths.log_dir — divergence on customization
body:
<!-- Task: t2917 -->

## Task

Make standalone runner scripts (`complexity-scan-runner.sh`, `efficiency-analysis-runner.sh`, future siblings) read `paths.log_dir` from settings JSONC at runtime — not hardcode `${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/` — so they stay aligned with the plist/timer install paths their schedulers configure.

## Why

Surfaced during PR #21070 (t2903) review by augmentcode (`setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1720`, severity: low). The launchd plist for `sh.aidevops.complexity-scan` hardcodes `${_xml_cs_log_dir}/complexity-scan-runner.log` for `StandardOutPath`/`StandardErrorPath`, where `_cs_log_dir` is resolved at install time via `_resolve_cw_log_dir` (reads `paths.log_dir` from `~/.aidevops/config/paths.jsonc` or falls back to `~/.aidevops/logs`). The runner script itself hardcodes `RUNNER_LOG_FILE="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-runner.log"` at module load.

If the user customizes `paths.log_dir` (e.g. `/var/log/aidevops`):
- Plist `StandardOutPath` → `/var/log/aidevops/complexity-scan-runner.log` (captures stdout/stderr from the runner process tree)
- Runner internal log → `${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-runner.log` (where `_runner_log INFO ...` writes)

Two different files. Operator troubleshooting may look in only one, miss half the signal. Confirmed framework-wide pattern: `efficiency-analysis-runner.sh:45` does the same (`readonly LOGS_DIR="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs"`).

This is **not a t2903 regression** — t2903 followed the existing convention. It is a latent framework concern that the t2903 review surfaced. Fix it once, in a shared resolver runners can source.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/complexity-scan-runner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/efficiency-analysis-runner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` (new resolver function)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-constants-log-dir.sh` (NEW — regression coverage)

### Reference Pattern

Three steps:

**1. Add `_resolve_log_dir` to `shared-constants.sh`** — a runtime version of `_resolve_cw_log_dir` (which currently lives in `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` and isn't sourceable from runners). Model on the existing function at `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1541-1559`:

```bash
# Resolve the canonical aidevops log directory at runtime.
# Reads paths.log_dir from ~/.aidevops/config/paths.jsonc when available,
# falls back to ~/.aidevops/logs. Tilde-expansion handled.
_resolve_log_dir() {
    local resolved
    if type _jsonc_get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        resolved=$(_jsonc_get "paths.log_dir" "~/.aidevops/logs")
    else
        resolved="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs"
    fi
    # Tilde expansion
    resolved="${resolved/#\~/$HOME}"
    printf '%s\n' "$resolved"
    return 0
}
```

Place it near the existing path-resolution helpers in `shared-constants.sh` (search for `~/.aidevops/logs` to find the right neighbourhood).

**2. Replace hardcoded paths in runners.** In `complexity-scan-runner.sh:81`:

```bash
# Before:
RUNNER_LOG_FILE="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-runner.log"

# After:
RUNNER_LOG_DIR=$(_resolve_log_dir)
RUNNER_LOG_FILE="${RUNNER_LOG_DIR}/complexity-scan-runner.log"
```

In `efficiency-analysis-runner.sh:45`:

```bash
# Before:
readonly LOGS_DIR="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs"

# After:
LOGS_DIR=$(_resolve_log_dir)
readonly LOGS_DIR
```

(Note: `readonly` requires the assignment and declaration on separate lines when using command substitution — Bash 3.2 limitation.)

**3. Refactor `_resolve_cw_log_dir` in `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1541-1559`** to delegate to the new shared function. Keeps install-time resolution and runtime resolution behaviourally identical (same source-of-truth).

### Verification

```bash
# Default config — both should resolve identically:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/complexity-scan-runner.sh help | grep "Runner log"
# Expect: Runner log: ~/.aidevops/logs/complexity-scan-runner.log (or expanded)

# Customized config — set paths.log_dir, both should now point to the new dir:
mkdir -p /tmp/aidevops-log-test
cat > ~/.aidevops/config/paths.jsonc <<JSON
{ "paths": { "log_dir": "/tmp/aidevops-log-test" } }
JSON
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/complexity-scan-runner.sh help | grep "Runner log"
# Expect: Runner log: /tmp/aidevops-log-test/complexity-scan-runner.log

# Re-running setup_complexity_scan should also point the plist there:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/setup-modules/schedulers.sh setup_complexity_scan  # or via setup.sh --non-interactive
plutil -convert xml1 -o - ~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.complexity-scan.plist | grep -A1 StandardOutPath
# Expect: <string>/tmp/aidevops-log-test/complexity-scan-runner.log</string>

# Cleanup:
rm ~/.aidevops/config/paths.jsonc; rm -rf /tmp/aidevops-log-test
```

Add a regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-constants-log-dir.sh` that:
- Sources `shared-constants.sh`
- Sets `HOME` to a temp dir, writes a `paths.jsonc` with a non-default value
- Asserts `_resolve_log_dir` returns the customized path
- Asserts default fallback when no JSONC present

## Acceptance

- `_resolve_log_dir` exists in `shared-constants.sh` and reads `paths.log_dir` with `~/.aidevops/logs` fallback.
- `complexity-scan-runner.sh` and `efficiency-analysis-runner.sh` both use `_resolve_log_dir` instead of hardcoded `${HOME}/.aidevops/logs`.
- `_resolve_cw_log_dir` in `setup-modules/schedulers.sh` delegates to `_resolve_log_dir` (no behaviour change at install time).
- Regression test at `tests/test-shared-constants-log-dir.sh` passes.
- Manual verification: with a customized `paths.log_dir`, runner log path matches plist `StandardOutPath`.
- ShellCheck clean. Bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays, no `${var,,}`).

## Complexity Impact

Each touched function stays small (resolver is ~10 lines). No threshold concerns.

## Out of Scope

- Migrating other log paths beyond runner self-logs (e.g. pulse-wrapper has its own logging stack — t2917 is scoped to the runner-vs-plist divergence specifically).
- Adding `paths.log_dir` to the user-facing setup wizard. That's a separate UX task if anyone actually requests log path customization.

## Related

- PR #21070 (t2903) — origin (augmentcode review @ `schedulers.sh:1720`)
- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:1541-1559` — existing install-time resolver pattern to mirror
- `efficiency-analysis-runner.sh:45` — second instance of the same hardcoded pattern

title: t2918: Invert tooling/product priority boost so tooling lifts product
body:
## What

Invert the tooling/product priority score boost in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:166` so when both repo classes have dispatchable work, the tooling repo (aidevops itself) wins the tie.

Old:
```jq
(if $priority == "product" then 2000 elif $priority == "tooling" then 1000 else 0 end)
```

New:
```jq
(if $priority == "tooling" then 2000 elif $priority == "product" then 1000 else 0 end)
```

## Why

Tooling efficiency unblocks product development. The aidevops framework is the meta-tool that all product work runs through. A bug in the dispatch loop, the worker lifecycle, or the issue-sync flow halts every product repo at once. The reverse is not true — a product bug only blocks that one repo.

Operationally observed in this session: a managed product repo had ~70 dispatchable issues and the pulse correctly fed workers into them, but the `aidevops` framework backlog (38 dispatchable issues with `bug` and `framework` labels) often went under-served because the score boost favored product. With both repos competing for ~24 worker slots, a small priority adjustment shifts the equilibrium toward tooling-first dispatch.

## How

EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:166` — single jq line in `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json`. Swap the boost values: tooling=2000, product=1000.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh

### Complexity Impact

No structural change — single-token swap inside an existing jq expression. No function size delta.

## Acceptance

1. `grep -n 'priority == "tooling" then 2000' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` returns line 166.
2. `grep -n 'priority == "product" then 1000' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` returns line 166.
3. After deploy, an aidevops `bug` issue ranks above a managed product repo `bug` issue in the candidate sort (cross-repo dispatch order changes).

## Mechanism (why this is a tiebreaker, not a routing change)

The label-based component of the score adds 3000-10000 (priority:critical=10000, priority:high=8000, bug=7000, enhancement=6000, quality-debt=5000, debt=4000, default=3000). The priority boost adds 1000-2000. When only one repo class has dispatchable candidates, both old and new behavior correctly pick the available work — the priority boost is only decisive when both repo classes have candidates with the same label class.

## Dispatch-Path Classification

This issue modifies `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, which is in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`. Per t2821, dispatch-path issues default to `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive`. Implementing interactively in this session.

title: t2919: Move pulse plist install earlier in setup flow to avoid timeout-skip
body:
## What

Move the pulse launchd plist install to run immediately after `deploy_aidevops_agents` in `setup.sh::_setup_run_non_interactive`, instead of only running in the late `_setup_post_setup_steps` → `_setup_noninteractive_schedulers` block.

The late install remains as the canonical regenerate-on-change path; the early install is additive — it ensures the plist exists/is current as soon as the deployed scripts it references exist on disk.

## Why

The pulse launchd agent is critical infrastructure. Without it, the entire framework dies silently:
- No worker dispatch
- No issue routing
- No cross-repo coordination
- No completion sweeps
- No NMR auto-approval
- No deterministic merge pass

Currently `setup_supervisor_pulse` runs at `setup.sh:1173` inside `_setup_noninteractive_schedulers`, which executes AFTER ~25 other steps in the unattended `aidevops update` flow:

1. Migrations (5+)
2. Cleanup (5+)
3. Agent deploy
4. Validators, hotfix config, CLI install
5. Skill generation + scan (parallel)
6. Runtime config updates
7. Routine, privacy, complexity, canonical, task-id guards
8. Worktree exclusions
9. **`_setup_post_setup_steps`** (printer + cch-extract cache)
10. **`_setup_noninteractive_schedulers`** ← finally installs pulse plist

If anything in steps 1-8 stalls (slow brew tap, network-bound MCP install, large repo scan), the unattended setup gets killed by an upstream timeout (auto-update daemon, launchd, or simply runner reboot) and the pulse plist install never runs. The runner then falls behind the fleet because the pulse never refreshes the plist with new scripts.

## How

EDIT: `setup.sh::_setup_run_non_interactive` — insert an early plist install block right after `deploy_aidevops_agents` (line 992).

The deployed scripts the plist references exist on disk after `deploy_aidevops_agents` returns, so this is the earliest safe point.

```bash
deploy_aidevops_agents

# t2919: Early pulse plist install (see issue body for rationale).
local _early_os
_early_os="$(uname -s)"
if _should_setup_noninteractive_supervisor_pulse; then
    setup_supervisor_pulse "$_early_os" || print_warning "Early pulse plist install failed (will retry late)"
fi

_deploy_hotfix_config
```

The existing late call in `_setup_noninteractive_schedulers` remains. `_launchd_install_if_changed` already content-compares and skips reload when identical, so the late call becomes a no-op on the steady state — no double-install cost.

Failure of the early install is non-fatal: the late path retries, and CI/lint guards still flag genuine plist regressions.

### Files Scope

- setup.sh

### Complexity Impact

`_setup_run_non_interactive` grows by ~10 lines (comment block + 5-line install block). Currently 92 lines (counted via approximate grep). Post-change: ~102 lines, just over the 100-line `function-complexity` gate.

Mitigation: extract the early-install block into a small helper `_setup_install_pulse_plist_early()` (3-5 lines) so the parent stays under 100. This is the cleanest path and avoids triggering the gate.

## Acceptance

1. `_setup_run_non_interactive` calls a pulse plist install path immediately after `deploy_aidevops_agents`.
2. The install is gated by `_should_setup_noninteractive_supervisor_pulse` (respects user opt-out).
3. Early install failure is non-fatal (continues with rest of setup).
4. The existing late call in `_setup_noninteractive_schedulers` remains in place.
5. ShellCheck clean.
6. Manual test: with a stale plist, run `setup.sh --non-interactive` and observe the plist gets refreshed before the heavy setup work runs.

## Dispatch-Path Classification

This issue modifies `setup.sh`, which is NOT in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`. However, `aidevops update` invokes setup.sh in non-interactive mode and depends on it for self-update. Treat with the same caution as a dispatch-path file — `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive`.

Fix 6 correctness bugs identified by augmentcode review on PR #21112 (t2855 IMAP

- **Medium:** `cmd_test` fetches all messages (from UID 0) — expensive on large mailboxes
- **Medium:** `python3 -c` snippets in `email-mailbox-register-helper.sh` interpolate user input directly into Python source — quotes/backslashes corrupt execution or write malformed JSON

## Why

`linters-local.sh` blocks every commit to this repo with `File size: 56 blocking violations (threshold: 40)`. The gate's threshold was set when the count was lower; current count is 56 (52 shell + 4 Python). Each commit that touches any repo file (even a one-line doc fix) trips this and forces `--no-verify` or unrelated cleanup, neither of which is acceptable as a steady state.

Beyond CI friction, files >1500 lines:

- waste tokens on every AI-assisted edit (full-file Read becomes mandatory but expensive),
- accumulate dependency cycles that are hard to extract incrementally (pulse-merge.sh documents a 2-cycle co-extraction in its own header — that pattern should be the exception, not the norm),
- discourage focused unit tests because the surface is unbounded.

## How

Per `reference/large-file-split.md`: orchestrator + sub-library pattern, identity-key preservation, known CI false-positive classes, pre-commit hook gotchas. Each split is one PR. Children inherit `tier:thinking` because:

- function-grouping decisions need design judgment (cohesion, call-graph cardinality, future extension),
- identity-key handling for hash-based caches must survive the split,
- the existing nesting-depth gate emits false positives during the split which must be justified or refactored,
- the 100-line `function-complexity` gate and the 40% advisory threshold both fire on long functions that get extracted as-is.

check)

**Step 1 — schedulers.sh nvm/volta/fnm sweep.**

Insert a new "Step 4a" block in `_resolve_pulse_runtime_binary` BEFORE the existing fixed-paths sweep (line 221). Sort version dirs newest-first (`sort -rV`) so users with multiple Node versions get the most recent opencode.

- **Read (step 1, `$_persisted_file`):** if the persisted file points at an executable that fails validation, drop it and continue to re-resolve. This heals existing alex-solovyev-class state.
- **Write (just before `printf '%s\n' >"$_persisted_file"`):** only persist if validation passes. The legacy `/opt/homebrew/bin/opencode` fallback (line 242) MUST be excluded from persistence on Linux machines where that path doesn't exist.

## What

Fix `_acquire_lock` in `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` to detect and recover from stale lock dirs.

## Why

A stale lock dir at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/dispatch-ledger.lock.d` from April 3, 2026 silently disabled dispatch ledger registration for **24+ days** (~1.7M seconds). Every worker dispatch since — both pulse and manual — has emitted "Dispatch ledger registration failed (non-fatal)" warnings.

Operational symptoms observed during the 2026-04-27 GH search-degradation incident recovery:

- Lock dir mtime stuck at Apr 3 17:12 UTC for 24 days
- `mkdir` retry loop in `_acquire_lock` (lines 78-85) loops 50× × 0.1s = 5s timeout, then returns rc=1
- All 3 manual workers dispatched during recovery had to be backfilled into the ledger after manual cleanup
- 233 completed + 396 failed entries in ledger reflect this breakage

Root cause: the mkdir-based fallback path (lines 73-86) has NO stale-lock recovery. `pulse-instance-lock.sh` already has the canonical pattern (PID file inside lock dir + age-based force-reclaim via `PULSE_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S=1800`).

## How

1. `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh:66-88` — replace simple busy-wait mkdir loop with stale-detection logic:
   - On mkdir fail: read `${lock_dir}/pid` file
   - If PID alive: short retry loop (current behaviour)
   - If PID dead OR age > `AIDEVOPS_LEDGER_LOCK_MAX_AGE_S` (default 60s — much shorter than pulse-instance because ledger ops are sub-second): `rmdir` + retry mkdir
   - Write `$$` to `${lock_dir}/pid` after successful mkdir (mirror pulse pattern)
2. Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-instance-lock.sh::_handle_existing_lock` — lines 70-115
3. `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` — add regression tests

- [ ] Lock dir contains PID file after acquisition

title: t3000: dispatch-single-issue-helper: apply pulse-parity ceremony pre-launch
body:
## Task

Extend `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` to apply dispatch ceremony parity with the canonical pulse path before worker launch:

1. Apply `status:queued` (replacing whatever status is present) atomically via `set_issue_status`.
2. Add `origin:worker` and remove `origin:interactive` / `origin:worker-takeover` in the same edit.
3. Add the runner as assignee and remove any prior assignees in the same edit.

This mirrors `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh::_dlw_assign_and_label` exactly.

## Why

Discovered during the 2026-04-27 GitHub search degradation incident: 3 framework workers (#21406/#21407/#21408) launched manually via `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` did NOT receive the dispatch ceremony the pulse normally applies. Concrete failure mode:

- **Pulse double-dispatch risk**: with no status transition, the next pulse cycle saw the issue in its previous state (typically `status:available` with no assignee after the operator unassigned to clear a dedup block) — eligible for dispatch — and could spawn a second worker on top of the running one. I had to manually run `set_issue_status N slug in-progress` after each launch as a stopgap.
- **Origin label drift**: when the operator dispatches a worker via the helper after a `claim-task-id.sh` self-claim, the issue keeps `origin:interactive` even though a worker is now running it. Downstream auto-merge logic and the t2189 idle-handover both branch on origin labels — wrong label = wrong behaviour.
- **Assignee race**: if the issue had a different assignee (e.g. the issue creator), the dispatcher does not normalise to runner-self, leaving co-assignment ambiguity that confuses dedup layer 6 (the same class of bug `_dlw_assign_and_label` was hardened against in pulse).

The helper's top-of-file design comment names a trade-off ("deliberately bypasses 9+ post-claim gates — minimal smoke-test path"). But ownership claim is not a gate — it is the per-launch state mutation that makes a worker visible to dedup. The smoke-test argument doesn't apply.

## Correction from initial filing

This issue was originally filed asking for `status:in-progress` + an interactive claim stamp + ledger registration. After reading the canonical pulse pattern more carefully:

- `status:in-progress` is wrong — pulse uses `status:queued`. Workers transition queued→in-progress themselves when they begin work. Setting `in-progress` from the dispatcher is premature.
- Interactive claim stamps via `interactive-session-helper.sh write-stamp` are not applicable for headless workers — those only apply to interactive sessions. Workers are tracked via the dispatch ledger, which is already registered at line 578.
- Ledger registration already exists in the helper (line 578) — the visible silent failure during the incident was caused by the t2999 stale lock, fixed in PR #21428.

The corrected scope is just the pre-launch label/assignee atomic edit.

## How

body:
## Task

Add three new framework rules to `.agents/AGENTS.md` to address recurring AI-session failure modes:

1. **Capture-don't-advise discipline** — when the AI identifies a fixable issue, file it as an auto-dispatch task instead of telling the user about it.
2. **Turn-end brevity** — cap status/progress turn-ends at ~200 words, prefer markdown links over prose.
3. **Proactive memory storage** — store breakthroughs immediately (not at session end) so context-compaction can't lose them.

## Why

User feedback (Apr 28 2026 session):

> "you have a habit of telling me things that need doing, but not utilising the todo & issues pipeline to set the fixes in motion"
> "the amount for human reading at each ai turn end, it's a lot... maybe it could be more succinct, and give links"
> "preserving human attention (finite, fallible) and making sure ai takes on the things it knows and has proven it can fix"

Three failure modes observed in t3005 session:

- 4 framework bugs identified but not filed as issues (just listed in turn-end prose).
- Multiple 600+ word turn-ends with paragraph explanations the user could have clicked links to see.
- Lessons stored only at end of session — would have been lost if context compacted mid-stream.

## How

`EDIT: .agents/AGENTS.md` — add these sections under "Framework Rules":

### Capture-don't-advise discipline (NEW — applies before "Default: do the work")

When you identify a fixable issue (bug, gap, improvement, framework debt), DO NOT just describe it to the user.

- File it as an auto-dispatch issue: `claim-task-id.sh --title "<desc>" --description "<worker-ready body>" --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:standard,bug"`. Worker pipeline picks it up.
- Tell the user ONE LINE: `Filed as #NNN`. Link, no paragraph.
- Anti-pattern (the "advisory trap"): listing N framework bugs in turn-end prose without filing them. The user is busy; the framework has dispatch capacity. Use it.

Applies to: framework bugs, perf issues, missing tests, missing docs, bot review followups, ANY worker-dispatchable task. If genuinely architecture/policy (not auto-dispatchable), say so and ask explicitly.

### Turn-end brevity (NEW — strengthens "Tone and style")

User attention is finite. Every turn-end should:

- Be ≤ 200 words for status/progress reports. Hard cap.
- Use bare markdown links for actionable items: `[#21451](url) BLOCKED` not "PR #21451 was created and is now blocked because...".
- Group by action type — **Done**, **In-flight**, **User-action** — not narrative.
- Skip explanations the user can click links to see.

If turn-end > 200 words: cut. Ask "did the user need to read EVERY part?" If no, link instead.

### Proactive memory storage (NEW — strengthens "Memory recall t2050")

Beyond session-end storage:

- Store lessons IMMEDIATELY after any breakthrough or unexpected discovery — context compaction can wipe an unstored lesson.
- Store-while-fresh triggers: framework bug + workaround pair, race condition discovery, API limit hit + recovery, dispatch-path fix, anything you'd want a future session to know in 1 query.
- Cost is one `memory-helper.sh store` call. Skipping it wastes the lesson.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

### Complexity Impact

Adds ~80 lines of guidance to AGENTS.md. No function complexity impact (Markdown only).

- [ ] Each new rule has: trigger condition, action, anti-pattern call-out.
- [ ] Markdownlint passes: `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/AGENTS.md`.
- [ ] Sections fit the existing tone (no emojis, GitHub-flavoured Markdown, ≤ 200 words per section).

grep -c "Capture-don't-advise" .agents/AGENTS.md  # expect 1+
grep -c "Turn-end brevity" .agents/AGENTS.md      # expect 1+
